solutionSql:
SELECT 'duplicate scan ids' AS check_name, COUNT(*)::integer AS offending
FROM (SELECT id FROM staging_scans GROUP BY id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) AS dup
UNION ALL
SELECT 'orphaned scans', COUNT(*)::integer
FROM staging_scans AS s
LEFT JOIN shipments AS sh ON sh.id = s.shipment_id
WHERE sh.id IS NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT 'scans without status', COUNT(*)::integer
FROM staging_scans
WHERE status IS NULL
ORDER BY check_name;
ambiguities: The only blank is the join type. LEFT is the join that keeps unmatched scans. I filled it with LEFT (LEFT OUTER JOIN); no other text changed.
"Duplicate scan ids" counts ids, not rows. A NULL id group would be counted if one existed; no dataset has NULL ids, so this did not change the answer.
"Orphaned scans" counts rows, so a duplicated orphan would count twice. No orphan id repeats in any dataset.
notes: Results: sample (1, 5, 4), nulls (1, 19, 4), boundary (1, 13, 4). Rows are in check_name order. The starter's other lines were kept unchanged.
